text:
mike: Heads-up — we got a report from a customer that they saw 429s while our metering shows less usage than enforcer reported. happening during a traffic spike in eu-west :thinking_face:

sana: I traced it — enforcer deducted tokens locally and emitted events, but the metering ingestion lagged ~40–90s. by the time the stream landed, the reconciliation shows a delta.

leo: this is the classic optimistic-consume + async-report problem. enforcer is designed for low-latency rejects, but metering pipeline is eventually consistent. When ingestion lags you get apparent "over-enforcement".

anya: can we avoid hard rejects for short transient ingestion gaps? suggestion: short local lease + soft-fallback instead of immediate 429 for the first N bursts.

carmen: sketch: local token bucket with lease_ttl=5s, allow an extra 10% burst headroom if the events are successfully emitted to the topic; if we don't see backfill within reconcile_window (120s) then mark key for audit and apply stricter throttling.

mike: +1. need to be careful about abuse though — attackers could exploit the headroom. maybe tie headroom to org reputation or paid tier.

leo: config example for enforcer:
```
{
  "burst_tokens": 200,
  "lease_ttl_s": 5,
  "reconcile_window_s": 120,
  "fallback_policy": "soft_queue",
  "tier_headroom": {
    "free": 0.05,
    "pro": 0.2
  }
}
```

anya: operational plan: feature-flag the optimistic-local-tokens behavior, canary on cluster-alpha (~1% of traffic), watch two metrics: (1) enforcer 429s vs ingested tokens mismatch, (2) post-reconcile account freeze events.

metering-bot: alert configured: `Alert:metering.enforcer_mismatch` -> fires when rolling 5m mismatch > 0.5% and >100 tokens. current firing rate: 0.3/day.

carmen: replay/playbook for missing events:
```
# quick replay
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --group replay-consumer --topic metering.events --reset-offsets --to-earliest
kubectl create job replay-missing --image=internal/replay:stable -- env TARGET=backfill
```
If backlog > 10m messages we escalate to infra for partition reassign.

mike: UX/console changes: add a "pending-reconcile" state in Quotas dashboard for keys/orgs currently using local lease headroom. Show "projected vs ingested" token curves and a small CTA to run replay/backfill. Product will want a one-click backfill for org admins (requires auth).

leo: rollout gating: implement per-org cap on optimistic headroom, default 0 for new orgs, enable for long-lived orgs >30d and low mismatch rate. This minimizes abuse.

anya: tests we need:
- e2e with artificial ingestion lag (0s, 30s, 2m)
- chaos test dropping metering events randomly (1%, 5%)
- load test to verify no memory blow-up when local leases accumulate

carmen: reconciliation job ideas: run hourly job that replays last 10m events, then issue credits or retro-throttle if overshoot found. we should surface retro credits to billing and flag for CS if > 5% monthly.

mike: ownership: eng-platform owns enforcer change + metrics. eng-sre owns replay infra and alert thresholds. product will own console UX/one-click backfill. security: validate no new path opens double-spend.

infra-bot: deploy plan posted: feature flag `optimistic_local_lease` -> rollout: alpha(1%) -> beta(10%) -> prod gradual; rollback if `Alert:metering.enforcer_mismatch` > baseline * 3 for 30m.

sana: I'll prototype the enforcer change this week and wire the emitted 'lease_granted' event to metering.topic so we can track headroom acceptance.

mike: thanks. next steps: 1) prototype + tests (sana, leo), 2) dashboard mock (mike, carmen), 3) replay runbook + infra ticket (carmen), 4) product spec for one-click backfill (product owns). tagging @product for visibility. :eyes:

mike: filing a short RFC after the prototype with configuration defaults and abuse mitigations.

metering-bot: note saved to thread metadata: tag=quota-reconciliation, severity=medium.
